title: Living Well with High Blood Pressure
summary: Simple daily habits that keep your blood pressure steady — food, movement, sleep and monitoring.
content: Check your blood pressure at the same time each day and keep a paper log to show your doctor.
Aim for less salt: flavour food with herbs, lemon and spices instead.
A 20-minute gentle walk most days strengthens the heart without strain.
Take medication at the same time daily — a pill box and alarm help you never miss a dose.

title: Recognising the Early Signs of Stroke
summary: Remember F.A.S.T. — Face, Arms, Speech, Time. Acting quickly saves lives and reduces lasting damage.
content: Face: ask the person to smile — does one side droop?
Arms: ask them to raise both arms — does one drift down?
Speech: ask them to repeat a simple sentence — is it slurred?
Time: if you see any of these signs, call 000 immediately. Note when symptoms started.

title: Safe Exercise After 65
summary: Chair exercises, balance training and gentle strength work that protect joints and prevent falls.
content: Start with 5–10 minutes and build up slowly — consistency matters more than intensity.
Chair squats and heel raises strengthen the legs that catch you when you stumble.
Tai chi and slow balance work are proven to reduce fall risk.
Stop and rest if you feel dizzy, chest tightness or unusual breathlessness.

title: Caring for a Parent at Home: A Family Guide
summary: Practical advice for families: medication routines, home safety checks, and looking after yourself too.
content: Keep a shared medication chart on the fridge so every family member knows what was taken and when.
Remove loose rugs, add grab rails in the bathroom, and keep walkways lit at night.
Schedule regular home visits from our volunteers so you can rest — respite care is not selfish.
Watch for changes in appetite, sleep or mood, and report them to the GP early.
